findings.claim: How cells divide by mitosis and meiosis, plus osmosis, diffusion and active transport.
findings.truth: Meiosis is not in this unit. The spec puts meiosis in topic 4.6 (Inheritance, variation and evolution), which is assessed on Biology Paper 2. The lesson body never mentions meiosis.
findings.evidence: spec 2.2 Assessments: Biology Paper 1 = topics 1-4; spec 4.1.2 Cell division lists only Chromosomes, Mitosis and the cell cycle, Stem cells

findings.claim: In Required Practical 3, you investigate the effect of a range of sugar solutions on the mass of plant tissue.
findings.truth: The osmosis practical is required practical activity 2 in this qualification. Required practical 3 is the food tests. The spec also says salt or sugar solutions.
findings.evidence: spec 10.2.2 Required practical activity 2: investigate the effect of a range of concentrations of salt or sugar solutions on the mass of plant tissue; 10.2.3 = qualitative reagents food tests

findings.claim: In Required Practical 3, what happens to a potato cylinder placed in distilled water?
findings.truth: Same numbering error as F2: the osmosis practical is required practical 2.

findings.claim: You should know the food tests for AQA Required Practical 2:
findings.truth: The food tests are required practical activity 3 in this qualification, not 2. Required practical 2 is the osmosis investigation.
findings.evidence: spec 10.2.3 Required practical activity 3: use qualitative reagents to test for a range of carbohydrates, lipids and proteins

findings.claim: Practice question 5 is labelled '9 marks - Evaluate' with a nine-point mark scheme.
findings.truth: This qualification has no 9-mark questions. Each paper is 70 marks with multiple choice, structured, closed short answer and open response items; extended response tops out at 6 marks. The item should be a 6-mark evaluate question.
findings.evidence: spec 2.2 Assessments (Biology Paper 1: 70 marks, question types listed)

findings.claim: Practice question 6 asks the student to plan an antiseptic-versus-bacterial-growth investigation, with 'sterilise equipment' and 'dispose of bacterial cultures safely' in the key.
findings.truth: Culturing microorganisms is not in this spec at all (no agar, aseptic technique or zones of inhibition anywhere, and no such required practical). The question still works as a general working-scientifically item in an unfamiliar context, so it is not worth an edit, but it is not practising spec content.
findings.evidence: grep of the spec for agar / aseptic / antiseptic / petri / inoculate returns nothing

findings.claim: The rate of photosynthesis is affected by three limiting factors: light intensity, carbon dioxide concentration, temperature.
findings.truth: The spec names four factors: temperature, light intensity, carbon dioxide concentration and the amount of chlorophyll. Stating a definite count of three leaves the fourth off the student's list.
findings.evidence: spec 4.4.1.2: 'Students should be able to explain the effects of temperature, light intensity, carbon dioxide concentration, and the amount of chlorophyll on the rate of photosynthesis.'

findings.claim: Practice question 5 turns on the inverse square law; practice question 6 and two flashcards teach lactic acid going to the liver and being converted back to glucose. Neither carries a Higher-tier flag.
findings.truth: Both are Higher-tier only in this spec. The content_html handles this correctly: it wraps both passages in a higher-only div. The questions and flashcards have no tier field in this data shape, so the options are (a) leave it, (b) add a '(Higher tier)' prefix to the two practice question texts, or (c) drop the items. Recommendation: (b) for the two practice questions, leave the flashcards. It needs Tom's call because it changes question text for every lesson in this format.
findings.evidence: spec 4.4.1.2 '(HT only) Students should understand and use inverse proportion - the inverse square law and light intensity in the context of photosynthesis'; spec 4.4.2.2 '(HT only) Blood flowing through the muscles transports the lactic acid to the liver where it is converted back into glucose.'

findings.claim: The whole lesson: culturing microorganisms, aseptic technique, nutrient agar, zones of inhibition, crown gall disease, identifying plant diseases, and plant defence responses.
findings.truth: None of this is in this qualification. The spec has no culturing content and no culturing required practical, and no plant-disease section: the only plant pathogens it names are tobacco mosaic virus (under viral diseases) and rose black spot (under fungal diseases). Everything else here is separate GCSE Biology only. A Combined student revising this lesson is revising content that cannot be examined. Options: retire the lesson from this board, or keep it as clearly labelled separate-Biology background. The edits below take the second option and label every exam claim; the structural decision is Tom's.
findings.evidence: spec 4.3.1.1-4.3.1.9 (no monoclonal section, no plant-disease section); spec 10.2.1-10.2.7 biology required practicals = microscopy, osmosis, food tests, amylase pH, photosynthesis, reaction time, population sampling

findings.claim: In the separate biology specification, you need to understand the practical techniques used to culture microorganisms safely and aseptically.
findings.truth: The sentence half-flags the scope but still reads as an instruction to this unit's students. It must say plainly that culturing is not on the Combined Science course.

findings.claim: Collapsible heading: 'Required Practical: Investigating Bacterial Growth'.
findings.truth: There is no such required practical in this qualification. The biology required practicals are microscopy, osmosis, food tests, the effect of pH on amylase, light intensity and photosynthesis, human reaction time, and population sampling.

findings.claim: You may be asked to describe how to investigate the effect of antiseptics or antibiotics on bacterial growth.
findings.truth: Not on this paper. This is a separate GCSE Biology required practical.

findings.claim: You need to know specific examples and how to identify diseased plants.
findings.truth: For this qualification the student needs two plant pathogens only: tobacco mosaic virus and rose black spot. Identification of plant disease, plant defence responses and crown gall are separate GCSE Biology only.
findings.evidence: spec 4.3.1.2 (TMV) and 4.3.1.4 (rose black spot); no plant-disease section in this spec

findings.claim: Exam questions on aseptic technique often ask you to explain why each step is necessary.
findings.truth: A false exam claim for this qualification. Aseptic technique is not examined here.

findings.claim: Question 1 is labelled '1 mark - Recall' but its mark scheme awards two marks: 'prevents contamination of cultures (1 mark) by unwanted microorganisms (1 mark)'.
findings.truth: The stated mark total and the mark scheme must agree. A one-mark definition takes one credit point.

findings.claim: Question 3 asks for 2 significant figures; the key gives 'A = pi x 7 squared = pi x 49 = 154 mm2 (accept 150 mm2 to 2 s.f.)'.
findings.truth: Recomputation: pi x 49 = 153.94, which to 2 significant figures is 150 mm2. The key leads with a 3 s.f. answer and treats the answer the question asked for as an alternative.
findings.evidence: recomputation: pi x 7^2 = 153.938, so 150 to 2 s.f.

findings.claim: The whole lesson teaches monoclonal antibody production (hybridomas), pregnancy testing, cancer diagnosis and targeted therapy as examinable content, with no scope flag anywhere.
findings.truth: Monoclonal antibodies are separate GCSE Biology only. The word 'monoclonal' does not appear anywhere in this spec. Unlike lesson 9, this lesson gives the student no warning at all. Options: retire the lesson from this board, or keep it as labelled separate-Biology background. The edits below take the second option; the structural decision is Tom's.
findings.evidence: grep of the spec for 'monoclonal' returns nothing; spec 4.3.1 runs 4.3.1.1 to 4.3.1.9 with no monoclonal section

findings.claim: Monoclonal antibody treatment is an example of targeted therapy because it delivers drugs precisely to diseased cells while leaving healthy cells unharmed.
findings.truth: Healthy cells are not left unharmed. Monoclonal antibody treatment damages less healthy tissue than chemotherapy, but the lesson's own limitations list says these treatments cause unexpected and sometimes severe side effects. The sentence teaches a misconception as fact and contradicts an earlier key fact in the same lesson.
findings.evidence: internal contradiction with the lesson's own limitations section; settled fact that monoclonal antibody therapies carry side effects

findings.claim: Questions on monoclonal antibodies often ask you to describe the production process - learn the five steps in order.
findings.truth: A false exam claim for this qualification. Monoclonal antibodies are not examined on these papers.
findings.evidence: grep of the spec for 'monoclonal' returns nothing

summary: Board anchors verified in the spec: six papers, 1 hour 15 minutes, 70 marks, Foundation and Higher, Biology Paper 1 = topics 1-4. Two whole lessons are out of scope - lesson 9 (culturing microorganisms, plant disease identification, plant defences) and lesson 10 (monoclonal antibodies) are separate GCSE Biology content that this spec does not contain. The rest of the unit is sound: every equation, worked example and answer key recomputes correctly. The other fixes are two swapped required-practical numbers, a meiosis claim in a description, a 9-mark question this board never sets, a missing fourth photosynthesis factor, and a 'leaves healthy cells unharmed' misconception.
